source_reviews.independent_solution: For general center O, H(P)=O+k(P-O), k nonzero. If k=1 the identity fixes every point, line and plane. If k!=1 the equation H(P)=P forces P=O. A line through O maps onto itself; a plane through O maps onto itself. Conversely a line/plane not through O has a nonzero perpendicular offset from O, multiplied by k; equality of affine sets would require (k-1) times that offset to vanish, impossible. For arbitrary distinct A,B, |H(A)H(B)|=|k||AB|. Thus it is a displacement/isometry exactly when |k|=1: k=1 or k=-1, not just selected examples. k=-1 is central symmetry and qualifies under distance-preserving space displacement.
